item.title: Govt moves on Teesta Master Plan, feasibility study proposed
item.description:
The government has taken a fresh step toward advancing the much-discussed Teesta Master Plan, with the Ministry of Water Resources sending a Tk 23-crore proposal to the Planning Commission for a feasibility study on the project.
If approved, an international consultant will be appointed through competitive bidding to assess the technical and economic viability of the proposed interventions, including a new barrage, river training, dredging, flood control, water conservation and related infrastructure.
Water Resources Secretary Dr AKM Shahabuddin said the feasibility study would be crucial for taking the Teesta Master Plan toward implementation.
“The technical and economic viability of every component will be assessed through the study, and subsequent works for the main project will be taken based on its recommendations,” he said.
Planning Division Secretary SM Shakil Akhter said the proposal would be examined under the established procedure, taking into account the project's necessity, cost, potential benefits and feasibility.
“If approved, it will pave the way for appointing a consultant through international competitive bidding,” he told BSS.
The government has identified finding a permanent solution to the Teesta River’s problems and promoting economic transformation in the northwestern region as priorities. The BNP's 2026 election manifesto also pledged to ensure a fair share of water from the Teesta and other trans-boundary rivers, while stressing balanced regional development and greater use of the agricultural and economic potential of northern Bangladesh.
The proposed master plan envisages a broad package of river and regional development measures rather than focusing solely on a barrage.
It includes riverbank protection or river training along about 110 kilometres, dredging of another 110 kilometres of the river, and construction of 224 kilometres of flood-control embankments with roads on top.
The plan also proposes constructing or repairing 67 spurs and reclaiming and developing about 170 square kilometres of land.
Engineer Md Ruhul Amin, director general of the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), said the plan takes an integrated approach covering river-flow management, bank protection, flood control, irrigation and transport infrastructure.
The feasibility study, he said, would determine the precise locations and scope of the proposed works.
The proposed embankment-cum-road infrastructure could improve connectivity in riverside communities that are frequently cut off during the monsoon. At the same time, the embankments would provide flood protection, potentially combining two important infrastructure functions.
Dredging, however, would require careful consideration of the river’s natural behaviour. River expert Mohammad Ejaz said dredging should take into account sediment transport, water discharge and the river’s flow dynamics.
“Merely deepening the riverbed will not provide a long-term solution,” he told the national news agency adding that the feasibility study should identify appropriate dredging locations and determine how dredged sediment would be managed.
A new barrage is another major component under consideration. The government is examining the technical and financial feasibility of constructing another barrage on the Teesta to conserve water during the dry season.
According to Dr Md Ataur Rahman, a professor of Water Resources Engineering at BUET, the feasibility assessment must examine upstream and downstream flows, flood management, irrigation requirements, structural safety, maintenance and environmental considerations alongside water-storage capacity.
The Teesta is closely tied to the lives and economies of people in Rangpur, Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari, Kurigram and Gaibandha. Reduced dry-season flow affects irrigation and agriculture, while high monsoon flows contribute to flooding and river erosion, threatening homes and farmland.
Riverbank protection is therefore another key element of the plan, alongside proposals to strengthen river training and repair or construct spurs. The proposed land reclamation could also open opportunities for agriculture, infrastructure and other forms of local economic development.
Yet the scale of the eventual benefits will depend on the findings of the feasibility study, environmental assessments, final project design, financing, implementation quality and long-term maintenance.
For people in the northern region, the latest move comes after years of surveys, plans and expectations surrounding the Teesta. The proposed feasibility study does not mark the completion of the master plan, but it could move the initiative into a more concrete administrative and technical phase.
Several steps would still remain, including completion of the feasibility study and environmental assessment, finalisation of the project design, government approval, financing and field-level implementation.
If implemented, the Teesta Master Plan would extend beyond a conventional barrage or river-management project. It could bring water conservation, irrigation, flood control, erosion prevention, river training, transport, land management and regional economic development under a single integrated framework.

item.title: City scandal risks damage to Premier League's booming brand
item.description:
The Premier League has won a lengthy legal battle with Manchester City over financial impropriety, but the consequences could leave lasting damage for a league that has long since become the envy of world football.
City face severe sanctions after being found guilty of over 100 charges between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission exposing "sham" contracts to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion).
A hefty points deduction resulting in relegation, stripped titles and even expulsion from the English top flight have been mooted as potential sanctions.
But the damage may not be limited to City alone with an entire era of the Premier League now under a cloud.
A takeover in 2008 by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al-Nahyan, the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, transformed City's fortunes, but also the face of the Premier League.
The club's first top-flight league title for 44 years was one of the most iconic moments in Premier League history when Sergio Aguero netted the winner against QPR in the 94th minute to deny Manchester United the title.
Some of City's rivals have been quick to revel in their downfall.
"Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet," posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team that finished second to City in the 2011/12 season.
Yet there could be more lingering collective consequences for a league that has become accustomed to flexing its financial muscle to hoover up the best talent from around the globe.
Italy's Serie A once enjoyed that status in the 1990s.
Although it had lost some of its lustre by the time the Calciopoli scandal came about in 2006, Italian football has arguably never fully recovered in the two decades since.
That case surrounded club officials influencing which referees would officiate their games and led to Juventus being stripped of two titles and relegated to Serie B.
- Haaland exit inevitable?
The question is now whether fans will be turned away from the Premier League after feeling cheated over what they have witnessed over the past 18 years.
In total City have won eight titles in the last 15 seasons.
They rewrote the record books, becoming the first side to ever achieve 100 points and win the English top flight for four consecutive years.
All of those achievements are now labelled with an asterisk.
"If I was a player, I'd be 100 percent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it's cheating," said former Manchester United captain Roy Keane.
Despite the Premier League's spending power, English clubs have still struggled to keep the world's biggest superstars away from Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.
City's demise could also see the Premier League lose its marquee player in Erling Haaland.
"The Premier League is Britain's greatest soft power cultural asset," Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian sport, told AFP. "What happens when people start to question, 'what have I been watching all these years?'"
By contrast, the Premier League has argued the City case is proof of strong governance.
The league pursued and persisted with an investigation which began in 2018 despite City's best attempts to frustrate the process.
"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history," said the league's chief executive Richard Masters.
"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition.
"It is paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously."

item.title: Asian Games: Mustafizur’s costly over ends Bangladesh’s gold hopes
item.description:
Bangladesh’s hopes of winning the men’s cricket gold medal at the Asian Games ended on Thursday after Pakistan beat them by six wickets in a rain-shortened semifinal.
Bangladesh made 111 for seven in 13 overs after being sent in, but Pakistan chased down the target with nine balls to spare, reaching 112 for four in 11.3 overs.
The match was still evenly poised when Pakistan needed 36 runs from the last four overs with four wickets in hand.
But Mustafizur Rahman’s second over changed the game. The left-arm pacer conceded 23 runs, including five boundaries, leaving Pakistan needing only 13 from the final three overs.
Abdul Samad struck an unbeaten 30 off 15 balls and Hasan Nawaz made 27 not out off 22 as Pakistan completed the chase comfortably.
Bangladesh had made a strong start with the ball, reducing Pakistan to 17 for two in two overs. Mehidi Hasan removed Sahibzada Farhan before Nasum Ahmed dismissed Maz Sadaqat.
Saim Ayub then added 21 off 12 balls before Mustafizur had him caught off the final delivery of his first over. Mustafizur finished with one wicket but conceded 41 runs in his two overs.
Rishad Hossain and Mehidi took one wicket each for Bangladesh.
Earlier, Towhid Hridoy top-scored for Bangladesh with 42 off 25 balls, hitting four sixes and two fours. He came to the crease after Bangladesh had slipped to 21 for three.
Saif Hasan made 19 off 17 balls and Mosaddek Hossain scored 11, while Mehidi remained unbeaten on eight from four balls.
Sufiyan Muqeem took three wickets for 26 runs for Pakistan.
Bangladesh will play for the bronze medal on Sunday against the loser of Thursday’s second semifinal between India and Sri Lanka.

item.description:

Sakhawat Husain said it is impossible to build a prosperous economy without a healthy and strong population.
“Therefore, everyone involved must be more sincere in ensuring healthcare for people in remote and marginalized communities while upholding the dignity of the medical profession,” he said.
Director of the National Institute of Ear, Nose and Throat Professor Dr Hasan Zafar presided over the discussion.
Dr Zahirul Islam Shakil, secretary general of the Doctors Association of Bangladesh (DAB), Professor Dr AKM Azizul Haque, chairman of Bangladesh Shishu Hospital, and DAB President Professor Dr Harun Al Rashid also spoke at the event.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s first wife secures bail in suicide abetment case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday granted bail to Maksuda Islam, the first wife of expelled Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam, in a case filed over the abetment of the suicide of his second wife, Mariyam Akter.
The court granted Maksuda bail after Mariyam’s father and case complainant, SM Masum Billah, submitted a settlement deed and said he had no objection to her release.
However, the court rejected Gazi Nazrul Islam’s bail petition.
The matter came up during a bail hearing before Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah.
According to the settlement deed, notarised on Tuesday, Masum Billah said Mariyam did not die by suicide due to any provocation or actions by Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda, or out of anger or resentment towards them.
The deed states that Masum Billah initially filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman on suspicion that they had abetted her suicide.
It says he later learned through various sources that Mariyam had not taken her own life because of any provocation or actions by Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda.
Under the terms of the settlement, Masum Billah and his family will have no objection if Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda are granted bail in the case.
The deed also states that, after their release on bail, both sides will seek to maintain cordial family relations and cooperate as needed with the ongoing judicial proceedings.
The settlement concerns Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station Case No-16(9)26, filed under Section 306 of the Penal Code, 1860.
The deed was notarised by Notary Public ASM Hanif on Tuesday. Mariyam’s father, SM Masum Billah, signed it as the first party, while Md Abdul Hamid Morol signed as the second party.
Police recovered Mariyam’s hanging body from Flat 203 of NAM Bhaban in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar on September 20.
The door was locked from inside. With assistance from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), police broke open the door and recovered her body hanging from a ceiling fan. Several notes were also found in the room.
The following day, Masum Billah filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Obaidur Rahman, accusing them of abetting Mariyam’s suicide.

item.title: ICB’s golden jubilee: From five decades of trust to a new era of capacity
item.description:
Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (ICB) is completing five decades of its journey in Bangladesh’s investment and capital market landscape.
Established on October 1, 1976, the state-owned financial institution has played an important role in transforming savings into investment, providing capital to industry and business through bridge financing, and contributing to the development of the capital market by creating demand and supply for listed securities.
Established in continuation of the journey of democratic, economic and institutional development that began during the tenure of president Ziaur Rahman with national interest placed at the forefront, ICB has gradually expanded its role in response to the changing needs of the country’s economy.
Its contribution has gone beyond direct participation in the capital market. In 1977, ICB introduced investment schemes and margin lending, followed by the country’s first mutual fund in 1980 and a unit fund in 1981.
Over the years, these initiatives have helped create investment opportunities and channels for mobilizing long-term capital.
According to institutional data, ICB’s direct investment stands at around Tk8,900 crore, while indirect investment through various schemes and mutual funds is approximately Tk27,900 crore.
Around 238 companies have received support through these activities, of which nearly 80 have been listed on the capital market.
The activities have also contributed to the creation of around 20,000 jobs.
The Equity and Entrepreneurship Fund has emerged as another significant initiative.
As of June 30, 2025, Tk1,624.27 crore had been disbursed to 1,039 projects in the agriculture and ICT sectors, contributing to approximately 51,806 direct and indirect employment opportunities.
ICB’s five-decade journey, however, has also involved considerable challenges, including market downturns, high financing costs, liquidity pressures, declining asset values, provisioning shortfalls and maturity mismatches.
The government has already provided Tk1,000 crore to strengthen the corporation’s financial capacity.
As ICB marks its Golden Jubilee, the challenge is not merely to celebrate its past achievements but to prepare the institution for the economic needs of tomorrow’s Bangladesh.
Expanding into areas such as Alternative Investment Funds, ETFs, Sukuk, corporate bonds, SIP/CIP, REITs and infrastructure financing could open new avenues for long-term capital mobilization.
At the same time, stronger investment in technology, skilled human resources, research, risk management, digital finance, data analytics and corporate governance will be crucial.
The Golden Jubilee, therefore, offers an opportunity for ICB to build on five decades of institutional trust and evolve into a more modern, diversified and sustainable institution—capable of turning savings into productive capital and helping shape the markets of Bangladesh’s future.

item.title: Power Ministry, HSBC & Carbon Trust initiate National Energy Study
item.description:
The Power Division under Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, HSBC and The Carbon Trust gathered to initiate the proposed “National Energy Study for Bangladesh”, a study aimed at supporting the country’s long-term energy security and transition towards a more sustainable and resilient energy system.
The meeting was chaired by KM Ali Reza, additional secretary, Renewable Energy Wing, Power Division, and attended by representatives from relevant ministries from the government, HSBC, and the Carbon Trust team.
The study aims to explore practical pathways to building a more affordable, reliable and sustainable energy system.
It will assess Bangladesh's current energy landscape, examine future electricity needs, and evaluate how technologies such as renewable energy, energy storage and other low carbon solutions could support long term economic growth and energy security.
Through analysis, stakeholder engagement and capacity building, the study will help inform future energy planning and provide a roadmap to support Bangladesh's transition to a resilient power sector.
According to the Ministry of Power, the study aims to identify cost efficient clean energy solutions for the Government of Bangladesh and potential pathways to attract foreign direct investment.
HSBC is supporting the study by working with governments and public-sector institutions to explore climate and energy transition solutions.
The bank has partnered with The Carbon Trust to support the study and provide training to help execute the plan.
Speaking at the session, KM Ali Reza, additional secretary, Renewable Energy Wing, Power Division, said: “This marks the start of an important study that will explore potential options for Bangladesh’s energy mix for Power generation. We welcome the partnership with the Carbon Trust and HSBC and look forward to identifying practical pathways towards a more affordable, green, reliable and secure Power system”.
Mahbub ur Rahman, chief executive officer, HSBC Bangladesh, said: “Given the current context, where the global energy markets face heightened uncertainty, this National Energy Study on Bangladesh is an important and timely initiative which HSBC is proud to support. As a long-standing partner to Bangladesh, we recognize that energy security is fundamental to the country’s sustained economic growth, competitiveness, and resilience. Through this study, we hope to support the Government of Bangladesh in shaping forward-looking and sustainable energy strategy, while supporting the long-term energy needs of our clients operating in the country.”
Andrew Lever, director, energy transition, Carbon Trust, said: “Bringing our global expertise across fossil transition, grid modernization and renewable integration we are looking forward to supporting the Government of Bangladesh in identifying pathways towards a prosperous, resilient and decarbonized energy future.”
The Carbon Trust is a global team of climate experts driven by the mission to accelerate the transition to a prosperous, resilient, low-carbon future.
It has more than 25 years’ experience connecting the dots across sectors worldwide, working alongside businesses, governments, public sector bodies, financial institutions and philanthropies.
The proposed National Energy Study forms part of HSBC’s broader approach to supporting key stakeholders in accelerating the transition towards a more resilient future.

item.title: Home minister: Crackdown on extortionists, criminals to be intensified
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday drives against terrorists, armed criminals, drug dealers and extortionists are underway and would be intensified further.
“Lists of terrorists, armed criminals, drug dealers and extortionists are always maintained by the police and regularly updated,” he said responding to a question from reporters after a meeting at the Secretariat on preparations for Durga Puja celebrations.
The police department is regularly collecting data on the number of terrorists, drug dealers and extortionists arrested, and the information is being published in the media, he added.
The home minister said the country’s overall law and order situation should not be assessed based on one or two isolated incidents, stressing that the government is continuing its efforts to ensure public safety and maintain peace in society.
“We have always told you this. We speak to the press almost every day. We are continuing our efforts to ensure the security of people and establish peace in society,” he said.
Asked about allegations of land grabbing and extortion using political influence, Salahuddin said the government considers a criminal a criminal irrespective of political identity.
He said police respond immediately to calls made to the national emergency service 999, go to the spot, make arrests and file cases.
“Whoever is involved, strict action will be taken against them and is being taken,” he said.
Asked about the role of a former lawmaker in an incident in Mirpur, the Home Minister said the matter is under investigation.
Regarding the incident at Radda Clinic, he said negligence of duty has been found on the part of a police officer. “The officer was immediately withdrawn and departmental action has been initiated against him.”
The minister also said there was no political involvement in the Radda MCH-FP center incident.
However, he said some of those involved in crimes might have political identities, but the government was taking legal action against them without considering their political affiliations.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,108 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,108.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,007, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The four new suspected fatalities were reported across four divisions; Dhaka, Sylhet, Chittagong, and Mymensingh with one death each.
A total of 1,221 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 191,731.
During the same period, 128 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,520.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 169,800 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 162,873 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Home minister: Coordination gap during eviction drive might be behind Mirpur clash
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Wednesday said a lack of coordination among the authorities responsible for the hawker eviction drive could be behind clashes at Mirpur in the capital when a police vehicle and three city corporation vehicles were set on fire.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from reporters after a meeting at the Secretariat on preparations for celebrating Durga Puja.
Asked whether there was prior intelligence about the city corporation’s plan to conduct the eviction drive with police support, the home minister said he had ordered an investigation into the incident.
“From what I have learned initially, I have ordered an investigation. I learned that the magistrate responsible and the officials from the city corporation or RAJUK did not properly communicate with the police. I think there was a lack of coordination,” he said.
He added that the matter would be investigated further.
A clash broke out between hawkers, Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) officials and police during an eviction drive at Mirpur in the capital on Wednesday.
The eviction drive began around 10am from Mirpur-10 to Mirpur-14 as part of the DNCC’s efforts to clear footpaths and roads of illegal encroachments.
At one stage, the hawkers clashed with city corporation officials and law enforcement personnel.
A city corporation vehicle was set on fire and a police vehicle was vandalized during the clash, said witnesses.
Several media workers were also attacked allegedly by the hawkers while covering the incident.

item.title: PM Tarique to visit Feni Thursday, inaugurate Muhuri-Kohua project
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to visit Feni on Thursday, joining several programs in Parshuram and Fulgazi upazilas throughout the day.
It will be his first visit to Feni since becoming the prime minister.
Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Md Suzauddhowla (Sujon Mahmood) said the prime minister will leave his Gulshan's residence for Parshuram upazila by road at 8:30am.
He will attend the inauguration and exchange-of-greetings program for the rehabilitation of the Muhuri-Kohua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project (Phase I) on the outskirts of Parshuram upazila and the Kheyaghat Ghat-Muhuri Bridge area around 12:30pm.
Tarique Rahman will attend a tree-planting program on Begum Khaleda Zia Women’s College premises in Fulgazi at 1:30pm.
Then he will visit the Fulgazi District Council Dak Bungalow and inaugurate the operation to supply electricity to the national grid from the rooftop solar power system installed there.
He will later rest and offer prayers at the Dak Bungalow.
The prime minister will attend a program at Fulgazi Government Pilot High School field at 3:30 PM for distributing Family Cards and Farmer Cards and providing honorariums to mosque imams, muezzins, khadims and people working at other religious places of worship.
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) approved the Muhuri-Kohua Flood Control, Drainage and Irrigation Project (Phase I) project in Parshuram on June 16 at an estimated cost of Tk 1,542.16 crore.
Under the project, rivers and water bodies will be re-excavated, flood-control embankments rehabilitated, riverbanks protected and irrigation infrastructure renovated.
The project includes rehabilitation of 67.92 kilometers of embankments, protection of 11.73 kilometers of riverbanks, re-excavation of 83.50 kilometers of rivers and water bodies, rehabilitation of 27 irrigation structures and construction of 77 inlets.
In the next phase, there are plans to construct new embankments along the Muhuri and Kohua rivers, as well as construct embankments along the Silonia River and carry out its excavation and rehabilitation.
The project is expected to be completed by 2030.
The prime minister’s visit to Feni was originally scheduled for September 17 but was later postponed and rescheduled for October 1.

item.title: BFIU seeks bank account details of Salman Muqtadir
item.description:
The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) has sought details of bank accounts held in the name of content creator Salman Muqtadir.
A letter was sent to banks and financial institutions across the country on Wednesday, with officials from several banks confirming receipt of the letter.
The BFIU has requested account opening forms, Know Your Customer (KYC) documents, transaction records and other relevant information related to accounts held in Salman’s name. Banks have been instructed to provide the information within a specified timeframe.
It was not immediately clear why the BFIU sought the information.
The request comes amid ongoing discussions surrounding an attack, vandalism and looting at Salman Muqtadir’s Brownfish Studio at New Guinea Properties in the capital’s ECB Chattar area.
The studio was attacked on Saturday night, causing extensive damage. The New Guinea Properties office and several nearby structures were also reportedly vandalized.
Saiful Islam Bhuiyan, a director of New Guinea Properties, filed a case with Cantonment police station over the incident, accusing the attackers of trespassing, vandalism, looting and theft. Police and the Detective Branch (DB) have arrested several people in connection with the case.
Following the attack, Salman Muqtadir initially alleged that it was related to extortion.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed later said a preliminary investigation indicated that the incident stemmed from a dispute over around 35 kathas of land.
According to the home minister, the dispute involved New Guinea Properties and a party linked to a retired military officer. Salman’s studio, located on the premises, was also targeted during the attack.
The home minister also said spent bullet casings and locally made weapons were recovered from the scene.
Police have also linked the attack to the land dispute, saying a group of people attacked the property following a conflict over its entrance and access routes. Some of those arrested have also been accused of being involved in planning the attack.
Following the home minister’s remarks, Salman said he had gone to Cantonment police station on the night of the incident to file a case.
He alleged that police were initially reluctant to register the case, although it was eventually accepted. His statements on the matter have been reported by several media outlets.
On September 29, Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Zahed Ur Rahman also mentioned Salman by name, saying content creators with large audiences should exercise greater responsibility in their future conduct.
Against the backdrop of the attack, the land dispute and the subsequent statements, the BFIU’s request for information on Salman’s bank accounts has drawn attention.
Sources said banks will now provide the requested account, transaction and related financial information to the BFIU as instructed.

item.title: Clash during Mirpur footpath eviction drive, vehicle set on fire
item.description:
Clashes, vandalism and arson broke out in the capital’s Mirpur-10 area on Wednesday afternoon during a drive to clear footpaths of encroachment.
A vehicle of Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) was reportedly set on fire, while a police vehicle and an excavator used in the drive were also vandalized.
Md Shahidul Islam, duty officer at Mirpur Model Police Station, confirmed the incident and said law enforcement personnel were working to bring the situation under control.
Police said hawkers had long occupied footpaths in the Mirpur-10 area, operating temporary shops and businesses.
The city corporation launched the drive to remove the encroachments. At the start of the operation, an argument broke out between hawkers and city corporation workers, eventually leading to clashes and counter-chases.
Vandalism and arson were reported at several locations during the unrest.
Witnesses said a city corporation vehicle was set on fire during the clash. A police vehicle and an excavator used in the eviction drive were also reportedly vandalized.
Initial information suggested that a fire first broke out at one location due to an electrical short circuit while the drive was under way. Later, some agitated hawkers allegedly set fire to a city corporation garbage truck.
Two Fire Service units responded to the incident and brought the blaze under control.
Additional police were deployed in the area following the incident, with law enforcement personnel remaining on alert to maintain public safety and traffic movement.
The drive was part of the city corporation’s regular efforts to clear footpaths of encroachment, officials said.
Police said those involved in the incident would be investigated and necessary action taken.

item.title: Malaysia's ex-PM Mahathir in hospital for observation
item.description:
Malaysia's 101-year-old former prime minister Mahathir Mohamad has been hospitalised for observation, his aide told AFP, following the death on Monday of his wife of seven decades.
The two-time prime minister was admitted to the National Heart Institute in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday night, aide Sufi Yusoff said, though the reason for his hospitalisation was not immediately known pending an official diagnosis.
Sufi said Mahathir had not been getting enough rest following the passing of his wife, Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, on Monday and was feeling fatigued.
"He is in a stable condition," Sufi told AFP in a WhatsApp message on Wednesday.
"He is exhausted from the emotional ups and downs, the hot weather and lack of rest. All of that is not a good combination for someone who is 101 years old," he added.
His wife Siti Hasmah, who was a medical doctor and an advocate for public health, passed away at the age of 100. The couple raised seven children together.
Mahathir, visibly grief-stricken by her death, told the country's former king through tears that he "didn't expect her to die today", in footage recorded at her funeral and posted on his official Instagram account.
Mahathir has suffered several heart problems in recent years and underwent bypass surgeries.
The centenarian has been hospitalised repeatedly in recent years, and most recently in January after suffering a hip fracture in a fall.
He has been dubbed the world's oldest-serving leader after helming office twice, first holding the position as the Southeast Asian country's fourth national leader from 1981 until 2003.
He then served as prime minister for a second time at the age of 92 from 2018 to 2020.

item.title: Gold prices rise
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has raised gold prices in the domestic market, with the price of 22-carat hallmarked gold increasing by Tk190 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold is priced at Tk19,785 per gram, up from Tk19,595 on Tuesday.
Bajus said the new rates were set after considering the overall market situation, particularly the rise in the price of pure gold (tejabi gold).
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Wednesday and will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring at 9am on September 30.
Under the new rates, 21-carat gold is priced at Tk18,895 per gram, while 18-carat gold is priced at Tk16,225 per gram. Gold made using the traditional method is priced at Tk13,255 per gram.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk230,781. Making charges will be added separately, depending on the design of the jewellery.
The price of 22-carat gold was Tk19,595 per gram on September 29, meaning the price per bhori has increased by approximately Tk2,214.
Bajus had reduced gold prices several times before the latest increase. On September 28, 22-carat gold was priced at Tk19,785 per gram, while the price stood at Tk19,970 per gram on September 26.
Bajus has also increased silver prices.
The price of 22-carat silver has been set at Tk370 per gram, while 21-carat silver is priced at Tk355, 18-carat silver at Tk305 and traditional-method silver at Tk230 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk355 per gram on September 29, representing an increase of Tk15 per gram.
According to a Bajus notification, VAT is included in the fixed selling price and cannot be collected separately from customers.
Making charges, however, will apply separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
For the exchange of old gold jewellery, a 12% deduction applies, excluding making charges and stone costs. An 18% deduction applies when purchasing old gold jewellery.
Bajus said VAT cannot be deducted separately in cases of exchange or purchase.
The fixed prices will remain effective at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.

item.title: HC questions why three women were stopped from travelling abroad
item.description:
The High Court on Tuesday issued a rule questioning the legality of preventing three adult women from travelling to Nepal despite having valid passports, entry permits and flight tickets.
The court also directed the concerned additional inspector general of police to investigate the complaints about the incident at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on August 8 and take necessary measures within seven days. It ordered the police to submit a compliance report.
The court further directed immigration authorities not to obstruct the three women from travelling abroad in future without a lawful basis.
The bench of Justice KM Kamrul Kader and Justice Fatema Anwar passed the order after hearing a writ petition filed by Rifa Tamanna, Sohani Islam Somapty and Najnin.
The three women, who are involved with the Bangladesh International Mediation Society (BIMS), were travelling to Nepal on August 8 as mediators to attend a conference, said their lawyer Ishrat Hasan.
She said Nepal provides visas on arrival to Bangladeshi citizens and that travellers from Bangladesh only need an Electronic Travel Authorization.
According to the petition, immigration officials stopped the women despite having the required documents, allegedly because they were unmarried and travelling without their parents or guardians.
In the rule, the court asked why the authorities’ actions should not be declared illegal.
It also asked why guidelines should not be formulated to ensure that adult women are not prevented from travelling abroad lawfully because they are unmarried, travelling without their parents or guardians, or on similar gender-based grounds.
The secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs, the inspector general of police, an additional inspector general of police, Police Headquarters and the immigration officials concerned have been made respondents to the rule.
Advocate Ishrat Hasan appeared for the petitioners, assisted by lawyer Tanzila Rahman Jui. Additional Attorney General Mohammad Arshadur Rouf opposed the writ petition.

item.title: Daraz Bangladesh extends support to flood-affected families beyond immediate relief
item.description:
Bangladesh has always lived with water. The monsoon feeds its fields and shapes its villages, and every so often floodwaters leave homes, possessions and livelihoods damaged in their wake. Emergency relief may address the immediate need, but for affected families, recovery continues long after the water recedes.
Over 12 years in Bangladesh, Daraz has built a nationwide ecosystem connecting customers, sellers and communities across the country. That presence has also shaped how the company approaches support for communities affected by natural disasters, extending its role beyond immediate emergency assistance.
This approach informed Daraz's response to this year's monsoon floods in Moulvibazar in Sylhet and in Satkania and Banshkhali in Chattogram.
The company committed approximately $30,000, around Tk36 lakh, to a multi-phase program covering three areas, essential relief for more than 900 families, targeted rehabilitation support for households identified as requiring further assistance, and flood-safety awareness for a further 1,000 families.
The relief packages, containing dry food, hygiene essentials and first-aid items, were the first step.
The program then moved into a more targeted rehabilitation phase. Alongside the distribution, Daraz volunteers spoke with affected families to assess the extent of damage and identify households requiring additional support. Those households received assistance based on their individual needs, including roofing sheets and bamboo for repairing damaged shelters, bedding and mosquito nets, cooking stoves and utensils, and safe-drinking-water supplies.
Kamrul Hasan, chief commercial officer of Daraz Bangladesh, said: "Daraz is part of many families' everyday lives, and when those families face a disaster, standing beside them is our responsibility. Relief is where we begin, and helping people rebuild is what we are committed to."
The people doing the work were Daraz's own. 20 colleagues from 5 department volunteered, sorting supplies, travelling to the affected areas and listening to families. "Our colleagues are members of these communities too," said Syed Abdullah Morshed, Chief People Officer of Daraz Bangladesh. "Participation was voluntary, and colleagues chose to give their time to support affected families directly. Their involvement reflects the sense of responsibility our people feel towards the communities in which we operate."
On the ground, project coordinator Sayem Hossain led the assessment work. "In Satkania and Banshkhali, we walked through neighbourhoods where the water had gone but its marks were everywhere, mud lines high on the walls, tin roofs and bamboo fences bent or washed away, bedding and cooking pots lost," he said. "The families were not asking for much. They wanted a livable place to sleep, a roof they could trust and something to cook on. We sat in courtyards and asked each family what they had lost. Some homes needed a new roof, others needed only bedding. Deciding who needed help most was hard, because everyone had lost something."
This is not Daraz's first response to a natural disaster. In 2024, the company reached more than 85,000 flood-affected people across multiple districts. While that response focused on providing immediate assistance at scale, this year's program introduces a more targeted rehabilitation component.
For Daraz Bangladesh, the program reflects a broader shift from responding only to the immediate consequences of a disaster to supporting recovery and preparedness as well.
For the families in Moulvibazar, Satkania and Banshkhali, that means support extending beyond the distribution of emergency supplies to rebuilding homes, restoring basic household needs and helping communities prepare for future flooding.

item.title: Honor introduces its connected ecosystem vision at Honor Connect
item.description:
Honor Bangladesh showcased its latest developments in AI and connected technology at Honor Connect on September 29. Held at the United Convention Center in Dhaka, the event highlighted the company’s expansion beyond smartphones into a broader connected ecosystem.
The Robot Phone made its local introduction at the event, alongside the unveiling of its new brand logo.
The program centered on Honor’s new “Dare to Be” philosophy, which reflects the brand’s approach of making technology more adaptive to people’s needs and more closely integrated into everyday life.
The company also announced Magic9 Pro's local arrival in the coming months.
Launched globally on September 28, the flagship is built in collaboration with ARRI, the cinema camera maker.
Filmmaker Raihan Rafi and cinematographer Sumon Sarker, who have worked on several prominent Bangladeshi film projects, attended as special guests and led a session on ARRI technology.
Speaking at the event, Honor SEA Region’s GTM Director Leo Pei said: “honor may have started as a smartphone brand here, but a phone is now only part of what we build. Our phones, tablets, wearables, laptops and TVs are designed to work together and adapt to how people use them.”
“People in Bangladesh want technology that fits naturally into their everyday lives, not technology that they have to work around. The Robot Phone is only one example of what the full Honor ecosystem can do, and there’s so much more to unfold,” said Lang Guo, country manager, Honor Bangladesh.
Mohammad Zahirul Islam, managing director of Smart Technologies (BD) Limited, said: “As you know, Honor is currently doing local manufacturing in Bangladesh, and our local manufacturing performance is on par with the best factories in the world. We will gradually bring Honor’s gadgets to the Bangladeshi market.”
“We have been serving customers through our partners since 1998 and have delivered millions of devices to customers so far,” he added. “We remain open to customers' advice and criticism, and we make necessary changes accordingly.”
Holding Honor’s Robot Phone, filmmaker Raihan Rafi said: “I felt that I could make an experimental short film with this. Our cameras are often very large, which limits the kind of shots we can get. This creates challenges in situations like shooting inside a car, among many others. One advantage I see in this camera is that we can place it anywhere and shoot. The camera movement is also very interesting. If someone is running, the cinematographer does not have to run with the camera. The camera can automatically capture it.”
Abdullah Al Mamun, head of business, and Syed Md Badrul Arifeen, director and head of product and marketing, also spoke at the event.
The event also featured an experience zone, where guests explored the brand's ecosystem products.
Alongside the Robot Phone, the lineup included Magic V6, Honor's latest foldable.
Other smartphones, tablets, earbuds, headphones and smartwatches were on display as well.
Guests also got an early look at the company's upcoming laptops and TVs, ahead of their arrival in Bangladesh.
These products are set to mark Honor's large-scale entry into both categories in the country, with a multi-series laptop lineup and TVs spanning 32 to 100 inches with the latest display technologies.

Health minister: Lifestyle changes needed to prevent heart disease
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has called for healthier lifestyle choices and greater public awareness as non-communicable diseases continue to rise in Bangladesh.
He made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a public seminar titled “Every Heartbeat is Life” at the National Heart Foundation in Mirpur, Dhaka, on Wednesday, marking World Heart Day.
The program was chaired by National Heart Foundation President Prof Dr Khondker Abdul Awal Rizvi.
The health minister said the government has taken several initiatives to bring healthcare services closer to people.
Work is underway to increase the capacity of all upazila health complexes from 50 to 151 beds, he said.
The government also plans to establish 10 dialysis centers at district-level hospitals and 50 at medical college hospitals, according to the minister.
These initiatives will help reduce pressure on hospitals in Dhaka and allow people in different parts of the country to receive necessary treatment closer to home, he said.
Sakhawat said the government had allocated the highest-ever budget for the health sector this year, stressing that improving healthcare infrastructure alone would not be enough without adequate manpower.
A nationwide recruitment process for nurses has already begun, while police verification of selected candidates is underway, he added.
The minister also expressed concern over rising HIV infections in the country.
He stressed the need to strengthen preventive measures and raise public awareness to address the growing burden of non-communicable diseases.
Textile and Jute Ministry Secretary Sharaf Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury, National Heart Foundation Secretary General Prof Fazila-Tun-Nesa Malik, Directorate General of Medical Education Director General Prof Nazmul Hossain and Prof Sohel Reza, among others, attended the program.

item.title: Yamal brace inspires Spain to Croatia romp, England down Czechs
item.description:
Lamine Yamal netted a brace as world champions Spain continued their winning start to the UEFA Nations League with a 4-1 success in Seville against Croatia on Tuesday, while Harry Kane scored as England won in the Czech Republic.
The match at the Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan was Spain's first home outing since lifting the World Cup in New York in July.
La Roja captain Rodri was handed the trophy by 2010 winner and Sevilla legend Jesus Navas, before presenting it to the ecstatic crowd.
"We were very excited to bring the trophy here," Yamal said.
"To be able to win the game and bring it home is great."
Spain's supporters did not have long to wait before their side provided further excitement in Andalusia as Yamal fired them into the lead inside 75 seconds.
Dion Beljo nodded in Ivan Perisic's cross to briefly level the scores shortly before the half-hour, but Atletico defender Marc Pubill popped up at the other end three minutes later to head in a Yamal centre and restore the hosts' lead.
After also scoring early in Spain's 3-2 win at Wembley against England last week to kickstart their Nations League campaign, Yamal brought his tally in the 2026/27 edition of the tournament to three as he put Spain two clear of Croatia in the 63rd minute with a precise finish at Dominik Livakovic's near post.
"Lamine is keen to keep developing and show the world the sort of footballer he is," Luis de la Fuente said of the 19-year-old star.
"We've enjoyed his magic in the service of the team. In the future, he'll be much more recognised for what he does and for his contribution to the team's play," the coach added of Yamal, who is among the frontrunners for the Ballon d'Or.
Nico Williams then put gloss on the result for Spain with a crisp step-over and finish with one minute remaining on the clock.
With two wins from two, Spain lead Group A3 on six points, while Croatia sit third on three points, behind second-placed England on goal difference.
In Prague, Thomas Tuchel's England got their first win of the group with a 2-0 victory over 10-man Czech Republic thanks to second-half goals from Anthony Gordon and Kane.
The home team kept England at bay in the first half at the Fortuna Arena despite being a man down after Pavel Sulc was sent off for a high challenge on Elliot Anderson in the 23rd minute.
"We played very professional, second half we stepped up... Deserved victory," Tuchel told ITV.
"Strange to get an early red card, not the best for the team and spectators. It's an awkward one but we kept going, got a win and that's what counts."
Barcelona winger Gordon broke the deadlock shortly after the break with a header from a cross served by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who made his first England start in almost two years.
It was Gordon's third goal in three games for England, including one against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final defeat and another against Spain.
Kane, who also scored against Spain, gave England breathing space in the 69th minute, smashing the ball past Czech 'keeper Matej Kovar after it fell to him inside the box.
England will travel to Rijeka to take on Croatia on Saturday, while Spain welcome the Czechs to Oviedo.
"The next match is important for us against a direct opponent and we want to win," Tuchel said to the BBC.
Elsewhere, Scotland paid for an early red card at Hampden Park against Switzerland as the visitors ran out 3-0 winners in Group B1.
Slovenia sit second in that pool after downing North Macedonia 2-0 in Ljubljana.

item.title: Sagar-Runi murder case report deferred for 130th time
item.description:
A Dhaka court has deferred the submission of the investigation report in the murder case of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi to November 5, marking the 130th time the report has been deferred.
Wednesday was the scheduled date for submitting the report. However, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), which is investigating the case, failed to submit it.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam then set November 5 as the new date for submission.
Sub-Inspector Rafiqul Islam of the prosecution division confirmed the matter.
The accused in the case are Rafiqul Islam, Bakul Mia, Masum Mintu, Kamrul Islam alias Arun, Abu Sayeed, security guards Palash Rudra Pal and Enayet Ahmed, and the couple’s friend Tanvir Rahman Khan.
Tanvir is currently out on bail, while Palash went into hiding after securing bail. The other accused remain in custody.
Sagar Sarowar, news editor at Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their residence on February 11, 2012. Following the incident, Runi’s brother, Nausher Alam Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
Initially, a sub-inspector of the police station was assigned to investigate the case. Four days later, the investigation was transferred to the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.
After more than two months, the DB failed to resolve the case, and the High Court subsequently handed the investigation over to the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) on April 18, 2012.
On September 30 last year, the High Court ordered the formation of a high-powered task force comprising experienced investigators from various agencies to investigate the murders. The court also directed that the investigation be completed within six months and ordered RAB to be removed from the investigation.
Following another High Court directive, the Public Security Division of the Ministry of Home Affairs issued a notification on October 17 last year forming the task force.
A four-member task force was subsequently formed, with the PBI chief serving as its convener.

item.title: Recommended primary teachers begin hunger strike in Jamalpur
item.description:
Fifty-one candidates recommended for appointment as assistant teachers at government primary schools in Jamalpur have begun an indefinite hunger strike demanding their appointment letters.
They took position on the second floor of the District Primary Education Office on Tuesday morning and started the program.
According to the protesters, 136 candidates were finally recommended for appointment in Jamalpur. Of them, 84 received appointment letters on September 24, while one received a letter on September 28.
The remaining 51 candidates have been left out despite, they said, having no legal complications or problems with their documents. The candidates said they would continue the hunger strike until they receive their appointment letters.
Shamim Yasmin Sumi, a candidate from Sharifpara village in Dewanganj, said she has to support her family as her elderly father has no income and her younger brother is unemployed. “My younger sister studies at a medical college and I have a small child. I was counting on this job to support my family,” she said. “I do not know why we have been excluded. My age is almost over for getting a job,” she added.
Muntazil Billah of Koalikandi village in Madarganj said he completed his bachelor’s and master’s degrees at Dhaka University before being recommended for the post. “We have been kept waiting for eight months. Of the 136 candidates, 51 still have not received appointment letters, but no specific reason has been given,” he said.
Sohel Alam of Mirzapur village in Jamalpur Sadar said the candidates were initially told they would receive their appointment letters in the second phase. “On Tuesday, one candidate received an appointment letter, but the remaining 51 were left out. We have no criminal cases, legal complications or document-related problems,” he said. “We want a clear explanation and our appointment letters. We will not leave until we receive them,” Sohel added.
The protesters’ presence disrupted activities at the District Primary Education Office. District Primary Education Officer Mohammad Ali Ahsan and other officials were not present at the office.
Contacted by phone, Ahsan said he was in Dhaka and working on the issue. “I do not yet know what problems the candidates may have under the relevant provisions. I have come to meet the aviation minister. They need to be patient. I hope there will be a positive outcome,” he said.

item.title: Dinajpur farmers incur losses as Aman prices fall
item.description:
Farmers in Fulbari upazila of Dinajpur are facing losses from early Aman rice as market prices have fallen below production costs despite a good harvest.
Harvesting and threshing of early Aman varieties have begun in the upazila. Farmers said rising costs of fertiliser, seeds, pesticides, irrigation and labour have pushed production costs above Tk20,000 per bigha.
According to the Department of Agricultural Extension, Fulbari has set a target of cultivating Aman on 18,150 hectares of land this season. Of this, 1,650 hectares have been planted with early-maturing varieties, with an estimated production of 8,415 tonnes.
The varieties mature within 90-110 days, allowing farmers to cultivate potatoes and later maize on the same land.
Farmers in several villages said they are getting 18-22 maunds of rice per bigha. However, paddy is currently selling for Tk750-Tk900 per maund, depending on the variety. This means farmers are earning around Tk17,000-Tk19,000 per bigha, resulting in losses of about Tk2,000-Tk3,000 against production costs.
Farmers said they are being forced to sell at the low prices to prepare for potato and winter vegetable cultivation, repay agricultural loans and meet household expenses.
Representatives of Fulbari’s rice wholesalers and mill owners said paddy prices have dropped by Tk200-Tk300 per maund over the past few weeks. They attributed the decline to adequate rice supplies and the availability of imported rice, which they said has reduced demand for locally produced paddy.
Shahanur Rahman, additional agriculture officer at the upazila agriculture office, said the department has no authority to determine or regulate paddy prices. “However, the government has provided farmers with free seeds and chemical fertilisers, along with necessary advice, to help reduce production costs,” he said.
The price gap has left marginal farmers worried about financing potato and winter vegetable cultivation in the coming season.

item.title: River erosion takes serious turn in Gopalganj, Satkhira
item.description:
River erosion at three points along the Shaildah River in Tungipara upazila of Gopalganj is threatening the 3-km Lebutala-Dumuria Road, disrupting travel for around 30,000 people in 10 villages.
Around 1,200 metres of the riverbank at Sarabari, Chithalia and Chhoto Dumuria in Dumuria union have been affected by erosion. Water Development Board (WDB) is dumping sandbags as a temporary measure, while locals are demanding permanent protection.
Several sections of the road have already collapsed, forcing residents to take 9-10km detours. Around 50 homes, farmland, a water supply tank, schools and religious institutions are also at risk.
“River erosion has already washed away my home and land. Now the road is also disappearing,” said Mohammad Shamim Molla, 60, of Sarabari.
Some van drivers said parts of the road have collapsed or sunk, making it difficult to operate vehicles. “In some places, we have to ask passengers to get off. Tyres get punctured, chains break, and bearings and motors are damaged,” one of them said.
College student Hridoy Sheikh said 3,000-4,000 people use the road daily, but ambulances, fire service vehicles and other large vehicles can no longer access some sections. “If permanent protection is not provided immediately, the road will disappear into the river,” he said.
WDB Sub-Divisional Engineer Mohammad Zakaria Ferdous said erosion was occurring along a 1,200-metre stretch at three points. “We are dumping sandbags as a temporary measure. A permanent riverbank protection project is being taken up under the South East Project,” he said, adding that the project would help prevent further erosion.
Meanwhile, a 50-metre section of Water Development Board (WDB) embankment in Ashashuni upazila of Satkhira has collapsed, putting 12 villages at risk of flooding. The erosion occurred in the Sripur-Kurikahunia area of Pratapnagar union.
Locals said water could enter residential areas if the breach is not repaired immediately, potentially flooding Pratapnagar and neighbouring areas. Part of the WAPDA road alongside the embankment has also collapsed, making the route risky for commuters.
Residents began emergency repair work on a voluntary basis, dumping sand and soil along the damaged section.
Abdul Khaleq, a resident of Kurikahunia village, said locals live in constant fear of flooding. “We have to struggle with the river throughout the year. Just as our homes, trees and crops begin to recover, we face another threat of flooding,” he said, adding that thousands of fish enclosures could be washed away.
Nur-e-Alam Siddiqui, a resident of Sripur, said that if this section completely collapses, Pratapnagar and neighbouring Anulia union could also be inundated. “We urgently need the WDB to intervene,” he added.
Ashashuni Upazila Nirbahi Officer Shyamananda Kundu said he had asked the local union chairman to begin preliminary repair work and informed WDB. “WDB will start work soon,” he said.
Abdur Rahman Tazkia, executive engineer of WDB Satkhira Division-2, said, “About 50 metres of the embankment has been damaged. We will start work as soon as possible,” he said.
Meanwhile, locals continue working voluntarily to prevent the erosion from worsening. They fear that without swift action, the breach could expand and cause widespread damage to homes, farmland and fish enclosures.

Morocco's king appoints Marrakesh mayor El Mansouri as first woman prime minister
item.description:
The king of Morocco on Tuesday named Marrakesh mayor Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri the country's first woman prime minister, the royal cabinet announced, after her party won last week's parliamentary elections.
Her centre-right Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) had dominated the vote, winning 97 out of 395 seats in the House of Representatives – 31 more than the next closest competitor, although the poll was marked by the lowest turnout in two decades.
The royal cabinet said King Mohammed VI has now tasked the 50-year-old, who also served as housing minister, with "forming the new government".
Without an outright majority, the PAM will have to form a coalition with other parties for its five-year tenure, though the monarch retains broad powers over major policies.
The PAM was founded in 2008 by current royal adviser Fouad Ali El Himma as a counterweight to the country's Islamist movement.
El Mansouri was also the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh, winning the office in 2009 before losing it six years later, then retaking it again in 2021.
El Mansouri's cabinet will have to tackle several pressing issues including unemployment and living costs, as well as persistent social disparities particularly weighing on young people.
"Young people are going through a crisis and we must provide them with answers," she said during the campaign. "We want to restore their hope, not only through speeches, but through concrete solutions."
Her government will also be expected to make billions of dollars in investments linked to the 2030 FIFA World Cup, jointly organized with Spain and Portugal.
The parliamentary vote came just weeks after tens of thousands of mainly young Moroccan migrants rushed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, a crisis that highlighted socioeconomic frustrations among the youth.
It also came a year after a Gen-Z protest movement took to the streets to demand better health and education.
Her party has pledged average annual economic growth of five percent, inflation of two percent and the creation of at least one million new jobs over its five-year term.
The PAM was followed in the polls by the National Rally of Independents (RNI), which heads the outgoing coalition and won 66 seats.
The right-wing Istiqlal party came third with 65 seats, while the Islamist opposition's Justice and Development Party (PJD) took 54 seats.
The PJD made significant gains after winning just 13 seats in 2021, having focused its campaign in part on fighting corruption.
Its chief, former prime minister Abdelilah Benkirane, hailed a "victory" but ruled out joining a coalition led by the PAM, which he said was "tainted by fraud", without providing details.

item.title: Govt ‘saddened and embarrassed’ by vandalism at Radda Health Centre
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has said the government is “saddened and embarrassed” by the vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur and allegations of involvement by members of the ruling party.
“The government is saddened whenever the rights of any citizen are violated, any facility is vandalised, or an individual is attacked. Ensuring citizens’ safety is the government’s responsibility, so such incidents cause embarrassment to the government,” he said.
He made the remarks at the Department of Information’s conference room at the Secretariat on Tuesday afternoon during a weekly briefing on the progress of government activities. He later responded to questions from journalists.
Asked what action would be taken if members of the ruling party were found to be involved, Zahed said: “Whoever is found to be linked to the incident through the investigation will be brought to justice.”
He said media investigations were important, but the police investigation would ultimately form the basis of the charge sheet.
“If the police confirm anyone’s involvement during the investigation, action will be taken against them as well,” he said.
Zahed said such incidents have a serious impact on the public.
“The state’s primary duty is to prevent crime. Once a crime has occurred, it is also crucial to ensure swift justice so that similar incidents do not happen in the future,” he said.

item.title: Man sentenced to death for raping 13-year-old stepdaughter in Dhaka
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sentenced a 43-year-old man to death and fined him Tk 5 lakh for raping his 13-year-old step-daughter in the capital’s Kamrangirchar area.
Judge Masrur Salekin of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal, also a district and sessions judge, pronounced the verdict on September 29. Bench Assistant Pankaj Peter Gomes confirmed the matter.
According to the case statement, the victim was a seventh-grade student who lived with the accused, her mother’s second husband.
On August 28, 2023, the accused allegedly raped the girl at their home in Nabinagar, Kamrangirchar, when no one else was present. He later raped her several times, threatening to kill her. The girl became pregnant and subsequently gave birth to a child.
The victim’s mother filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Kamrangirchar Police Station on the same day.
After completing the investigation, police submitted a charge sheet against the accused on January 23, 2025. The tribunal framed charges on August 24, 2025, and commenced the trial.
During the trial, the court recorded testimony from six prosecution witnesses. After examining the evidence and hearing arguments, the court found the accused guilty and sentenced him to death, along with a fine of Tk 5 lakh.
Under Section 9(1) of the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000, the court ordered that the convict be hanged by the neck until death.
The fine will be paid to the victim or her legal guardian. If the amount is not paid within the stipulated period, the court ordered that it be recovered by auctioning the convict’s movable or immovable property.
In its observations, the court said Section 9(1) provides two sentencing options for rape: the death penalty or life imprisonment with hard labour.
The court observed that Jamal Hossain had raped a 13-year-old child and that ensuring appropriate punishment for such an offence was its responsibility.
Citing a decision of the Supreme Court’s Appellate Division, the court said the crime was committed not only against the victim but also against the society to which she belongs.

item.title: IGP: Criminals to face action regardless of political affiliation
item.description:
Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir has directed police to take legal action against drug dealers, criminals and extortionists regardless of their political affiliation.
“There is no scope to consider an offender’s political affiliation. The only identity of a criminal is that he is a criminal,” he said.
He also instructed field-level officers to take appropriate legal action against juvenile offenders.
The IGP gave the directives at the monthly crime review meeting for August 2026 at Police Headquarters on Tuesday morning.
He said the police’s “zero tolerance” policy against drugs would continue and directed officers to take measures to prevent drug trafficking and the spread of narcotics.
He also stressed community policing and greater public participation in preventing drug-related crimes.
The IGP instructed field-level officers to ensure adequate security for the upcoming Durga Puja celebrations and take measures to prevent rumours and misinformation.
The meeting was chaired by Additional IGP (Crime and Operations) Md Sayedur Rahman.
Regarding teen gangs, the IGP directed officers to gather information on the gangs, investigate whether influential individuals were operating behind them and take legal action accordingly.

item.title: Child injured in gunfight between two groups in Sajek

According to local sources, the two groups exchanged several hundred rounds of gunfire over establishing control in the area.
Sanjita Tripura, a resident of Chailyatali, was hit by a bullet in her left hand during the exchange.

Sajek police station Officer-in-Charge Tofail Ahmed said the two groups exchanged gunfire in the morning over establishing control in the area.

item.title: Walton, MUN Alert launch initiative to help find missing people
item.description:
Walton Plaza, the country’s largest electronics product sales and service network, has stepped forward with a new initiative to help locate missing people more quickly.
In this regard, Walton Plaza, in collaboration with missing-person alert platform MUN Alert, has launched the ‘Missing Persons Broadcast’ initiative.
Under the initiative, photos and essential information of verified missing persons will be regularly displayed on TV screens at more than 700 Walton Plaza outlets across the country.
In this regard, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between Walton Plaza and MUN Alert at Walton Corporate Office in the capital on Monday (September 28, 2026).
Mohammad Rayhan, managing director of Walton Plaza, and Sadat Rahman, president of Zero Missing Foundation, the founding organization of MUN Alert, signed the MoU on behalf of their respective organizations.
Among others, Zoheb Ahmed, chief marketing officer of Walton; Masud Parvez, chief executive officer of creative partner Pop5, and officials from the organizations concerned were present at the signing ceremony.
Speaking at the event, Walton Plaza’s Managing Director Mohammad Rayhan said, “Walton Plaza has not confined its activities to product sales and services; rather, it actively participates in various social and humanitarian initiatives for the welfare of the people.
As part of that commitment, we have joined hands with MUN Alert to help disseminate information about missing persons quickly and extensively among the public.”
He said that under the initiative, people will be able to visit their nearest Walton Plaza to view the latest information on missing persons.
When necessary, they will also be able to report a missing person or follow up on an existing report through MUN Alert’s helpline 13219 and its web portal.
Walton’s CMO Zoheb Ahmed said: “A large number of people visit Walton Plaza outlets across the country every day. Using this extensive network and the TV screens at our official outlets to disseminate information about missing persons is part of our social responsibility. We believe this initiative will play an effective role in helping locate missing people quickly and supporting their families.”
MUN Alert founder Sadat Rahman said: “The wider the reach of verified information, the greater the possibility of finding a missing person. Walton Plaza’s extensive nationwide network will help take missing-person information to many places that would otherwise be difficult for us to reach on our own. We are delighted to have Walton Plaza by our side in this humanitarian initiative.”

item.title: Iran threatens new strikes as it awaits US response to Hormuz plan
item.description:
Iran on Tuesday threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric as it awaits a formal response from Washington on a new plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump has already dismissed the proposal from Tehran, but Iran’s foreign minister said Monday that he was expecting a formal response from American officials in the coming day.
Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Tehran has continued to target ships in the strait, with Washington falling back on an economic pressure campaign instead of further military action.
Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Tuesday threatened new attacks, saying no infrastructure in the region would be safe if his country’s security was not guaranteed.
“In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe,” Ghalibaf, who is also Iran’s parliament speaker, said according to video released by state TV.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he expected a formal answer from the US on Tuesday to Tehran’s proposal, state media reported.
Iran has maintained a blockade on commercial shipping through Hormuz since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic.
The shipping route carried a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas before the conflict began.
The US military has been maintaining a counterblockade of Iran’s ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting oil.
Araghchi said late Monday that Qatari intermediaries “presented ideas, and we discussed them; they are set to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response will be conveyed to us.”
The top diplomat, who was in New York for the UN General Assembly, said “The Qataris hope this will be done by tomorrow.”
“The current focus is solely on the Strait of Hormuz, and the reopening of the strait is contingent upon the fulfilment of certain conditions that we have communicated to the other side,” he added.
Last week, discussions were held in New York between Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade on its ports.
Both sides claim to have control of Hormuz, with the US saying oil is moving through and Tehran insisting the waterway is closed.
On Tuesday, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country’s military, said “the US claim that it remains open is false.”
“Sneaking a few hundred barrels of oil through under the cover of darkness -- with transponders turned off and at great cost -- does not constitute the strait being open,” said spokesperson Hossein Mohebi.
“A truly open strait is one where, as in the past, at least 125 vessels would pass through daily, transporting a minimum of 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products.
“Any vessel attempting to pass through sustains damage -- either we strike it, or it hits a mine,” he added.
